items.title: Open files from the terminal with `pandia`
items.detail: Install the command under Settings → Behavior. `pandia a.json b.json` opens both files as tabs in the window you already have, `pandia --diff a.json b.json` opens them in Compare, and `cat data.json | pandia -` opens piped input. See [the command-line guide](/docs/command-line).

items.title: Review piped JSON and send it back to a script
items.detail: With `--wait`, the command waits until you close the tab. Edit the JSON, press Save, and the command prints what you saved, so `pandia --wait - < draft.json > final.json` puts a person in the middle of a script. The exit code says whether the file opened, passed its schema or was closed without saving, and `--json` prints a full report instead.

items.title: Schemas load on their own
items.detail: Open a document whose top-level `$schema` points to a schema file or URL, and the Schema panel loads it and validates. `--schema` sets one from the terminal and wins over the document. Pandia asks before downloading a schema from the web, and uses only https:// unless you allow http under Settings → Behavior. Requested in [#27](https://github.com/hendurhance/pandia/issues/27).

items.title: Preview images inside your data
items.detail: Hover a value holding an image in Tree or Grid to see it. `data:image` values show at once. Links to images on the web ask before loading, or load straight away once you turn on “image previews from the web”.

items.title: Pull one key out of every item
items.detail: Right-click a key inside an array item and choose “Extract key from all items”. Pandia collects that key from every item into a new tab as an array, and skips items that do not have it.

items.title: Edit a key or value where it is
items.detail: Double-click a key or value in Tree to edit it in place. F2 does the same from the keyboard.

items.title: See what changed when you update
items.detail: The update prompt now shows the notes for the new version, with Install and restart, Later and Skip this version. If you update another way, a “what’s new” cell in the status bar opens them once. Help → What’s New shows every version.

items.title: A repaired file opens as a copy
items.detail: Repair used to put the fixed text in place of your file on the next Save. A repaired file now opens as `name.repaired.json`, so Save asks where to keep it, and the banner lists each change in a plain sentence, such as “Added a missing colon.”

items.title: Repair fixes more broken files
items.detail: `{"a" 1}` gets its colon back instead of losing the key, JSON Lines with a cut-off last line opens, a broken `\ud800` escape becomes �, and `NaN`, `Infinity` or `undefined` turned into `null` come with a note that says so.

items.title: Very large files take half the memory
items.detail: Opening a 524 MB file used to peak at 1.08 GB of memory, because the text was held twice. It now peaks at 553 MB, so a 2 GB file no longer needs about 4 GB free.

items.title: Grid reaches every row and finds every column
items.detail: Arrays of more than 1.4 million rows stopped scrolling before the end; the scrollbar now reaches the last row. A key that appears in only a few items far down the array now becomes a column, found by a scan in the background. On an array nested inside a 106 MB file, finding the columns went from 9.8 seconds to 0.18.

items.title: Grid shows `null` and filters text as text
items.detail: A `null` cell shows `—`, so it no longer looks the same as a missing one, and filtering a text column for `501` no longer matches `00501`.

items.title: Documents nested up to 1,000 levels deep
items.detail: Valid JSON nested more than 128 levels deep was called invalid, and some deeper files crashed the app. Every view now handles 1,000 levels, and a deeper file gets a plain message instead of a crash.

items.title: Compare shows what really changed
items.detail: Editing an item after an insert used to show the whole item as removed and added again. Compare now shows the insert and the one field that changed, updates as you edit either side, and keeps your place in the list.

items.title: Generated types compile in more cases
items.detail: Keys like `type` or `class` no longer break Rust, Python, Java or Kotlin. Java compiles as one file, IDs above the 64-bit signed limit get a type that holds them in every language, such as `u64`, `BigInteger`, `ULong`, `int|float` or `num`, PHP no longer writes the invalid `?mixed`, and Python dataclasses import with optional fields in any order.

items.title: CSV keeps your data as it is
items.detail: Importing keeps codes like `00501` as text. Exporting puts a `'` before text that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`, so a spreadsheet shows it instead of running it as a formula.

items.title: Theme follows your system
items.detail: New installs and Restore defaults use Auto, and light mode no longer flashes dark at startup.

items.title: File errors name the file and the cause
items.detail: When open, save or export fails, the message says which file and why: it is missing, you have no permission, it is a folder, it is not UTF-8, the disk is full or it is read-only.

items.title: Copy value and paste failed on Linux
items.detail: Copy → Value showed “The request is not allowed by the user agent…” and copied nothing, and Paste said the clipboard was unavailable. Copy and paste now go through the system clipboard directly. Reported in [#30](https://github.com/hendurhance/pandia/issues/30).

items.title: A failed edit on a large file could replace it with `null`
items.detail: On files of 10 MB or more, an edit that reached a deeply nested value or a broken emoji escape turned the document into `null`, and Save then wrote `null` over the file. A failed edit now leaves the document as it was.

items.title: Repair could change the text inside strings
items.detail: A path such as `C:\\new\\file.txt` came back with a line break and a form feed in it. Repair no longer touches escapes inside strings.

items.title: Replace All could delete a key
items.detail: Replacing `foo` with `baz` in `{"foo": 1, "baz": 2}` silently dropped one of them. A rename that would collide with another key is now skipped.

items.title: Restoring after a crash brought back only one tab
items.detail: “Restore all” reopened the last backup and deleted the others, and opening several files at once, by dropping three or with `pandia a.json b.json`, opened only the last. Every file now opens in its own tab, and a backup is deleted only after its tab opens.

items.title: Close Document discarded unsaved edits
items.detail: It now asks first, the same as closing a tab.

items.title: A crash during Save could leave half a file
items.detail: Save, export and crash backups now write to a temporary file and swap it in, so a crash or a full disk mid-write leaves the original intact. An export that fails no longer empties the file it was replacing.

items.title: Your last keystrokes could be skipped by Save
items.detail: A background save that finished while you were typing in Code view marked the tab as saved, so ⌘S missed what you typed after it. An unfinished edit in Code view was also dropped when you jumped away with Compare, Go to Path or the Outline.

items.title: Moves in Tree landed on the wrong item
items.detail: Dragging item 500 onto 499 moved it to index 231, an edit could save to another row after rows loaded above it, and Cut then Paste in the same array made a copy instead of moving.

items.title: Edits waited for a running comparison
items.detail: Comparing two large documents held them locked, so an edit could wait close to a second for the comparison to finish. Edits now go through at once.

items.title: Find and Replace opened Hide on macOS
items.detail: ⌘H is the macOS shortcut for Hide. Find and Replace is now ⌘⌥F on macOS and opens with the replace field showing; Windows and Linux keep Ctrl+H.

items.title: Text-field shortcuts on Windows and Linux
items.detail: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+V in a text field now edit that field instead of the document, and Ctrl+Z on a French AZERTY keyboard no longer closes the tab.

items.title: Find jumped back to the first match after every edit
items.detail: It now keeps your place, and an edit in Code view with Find open no longer switches you to Tree.

items.title: Graph cards overlapped and went stale
items.detail: A tall card no longer covers the one above it, the graph updates after Undo and Redo, and an error no longer replaces it for good. Arrays with thousands of items show a set number of cards and a “… N more” card instead of thousands of cards.

items.title: Grid view shows where newlines are
items.detail: A cell containing line breaks now displays a dim ↵ at each break instead of silently joining the lines. The row stays compact; hover or click the cell to read the full value.

items.title: AppImage accepted into the AppImage catalog
items.detail: The build was missing the `.DirIcon` file the catalog requires. It is now injected after every Linux release build, GPG-signed and re-packaged automatically.

items.title: Generate Dart models for Flutter
items.detail: Dart joins TypeScript, Rust, Go, Kotlin, Python, PHP, Java, Zod and JSON Schema in the Types panel. You get null-safe classes with `fromJson` and `toJson`, and no packages to add to your project.

items.title: Choose the view every file opens in
items.detail: Pick Tree, Code, Grid or Graph under Settings → Layout. Contributed by [@mcbyte-it](https://github.com/mcbyte-it).

items.title: Error messages tell you what to do about it
items.detail: `document too large: 2147483649 bytes (limit 2147483648 bytes)` now reads “This document is 2.00 GiB — the limit for this action is 2.00 GiB. Use a smaller file.” Every error keeps the technical detail a developer needs and drops the raw byte counts.

items.title: YAML, CSV, XML and cURL convert however the file arrives
items.detail: Dropping one in, opening it from the file picker or reopening it from recent files now offers the same conversion that pasting always did.

items.title: Files with comments warn you before you lose them
items.detail: Opening a `.jsonc` says the comments were removed in order to read it, and saving asks once more — with Save As offered so the original file survives untouched.

items.title: Scrolling holds its place in Grid, Compare and the Outline
items.detail: Rows arriving above the viewport used to shift what you were reading out from under you. The Tree already held its position; now every list does.

items.title: Exit moved to the File menu on Windows and Linux
items.detail: It used to sit at the bottom of Help, which is not where anyone looks for it. macOS is unchanged — Quit stays in the Pandia menu.

items.title: Auto-repair runs wherever a document fails to parse
items.detail: Not only on paste. The setting is renamed to match what it does.

items.title: Copy buttons say when the clipboard is unavailable
items.detail: Previously they did nothing at all.

items.title: Compare showed differences that were not real
items.detail: A file with a dozen small edits spread through it — 154 KB was enough to trigger it — reported every line on both sides as changed. Nothing warned you; the comparison simply looked like a full rewrite. Comparing is now exact at any size Pandia can open.

items.title: Compare refused any file over 3 MB
items.detail: That limit is gone. Both documents are now compared in Rust and only the lines on screen are fetched, so an 800,000-line comparison takes about 40 milliseconds.

items.title: Compare could report no change when a number had changed
items.detail: Any integer of 16 digits or more was rounded before the two sides were compared, so two Discord or Twitter snowflakes within about 128 of each other read as identical — and `10.00` against `10.0` showed nothing at all. Numbers are now compared exactly as they appear in your file.

items.title: Editing a number could silently change it
items.detail: Clicking into a value and clicking away without typing anything was enough: a 100-digit integer came back as `1.2345678901234568e+99`, and `1e309` came back as `null`. Every digit you type is now stored exactly as written, and undo restores the original text.

items.title: Editing a long string could shorten it
items.detail: Values over 1,000 characters are shown abbreviated in the tree, and if the full value could not be fetched the editor opened on the abbreviation — saving then wrote that over your data. The editor now refuses to open rather than risk it.

items.title: Grid filters treated two different big numbers as equal
items.detail: Two 19-digit IDs differing only in the last digit matched the same filter, and a number range rounded the bounds you typed before comparing. Filters now compare numbers exactly.

items.title: Copying a value could round a large number
items.detail: Copy value on a node holding a 64-bit ID put the rounded form on your clipboard.

items.title: The filter list showed large numbers as `{…}`
items.detail: Values that needed full precision fell through to the placeholder meant for objects, so you could not tell them apart or pick one.

items.title: Graph view would not open very large objects
items.detail: An object too big to count its children up front was drawn as a leaf, with no way to expand it.

items.title: Undo and redo left Find results stale
items.detail: Search hits kept pointing at the document as it was before you undid. Every edit path now refreshes them.

items.title: The theme setting did nothing
items.detail: The Dark, Light and Auto buttons only filtered which theme cards were listed below them; clicking one looked like a choice but changed nothing, before or after a relaunch. They now switch the theme immediately, and Auto follows your system appearance.

items.title: Three crashes while scrolling and editing
items.detail: Scrolling the tree while rows loaded in above you, clicking a row that had just collapsed, and expanding a gap in Compare while the diff reloaded could each fail and leave the pane blank.

items.title: Compare jumped back to the top while you were scrolling
items.detail: Scrolling quickly or dragging the scrollbar pulled the view back to the first difference every time new rows arrived.

items.title: The tree view could not scroll sideways
items.detail: Deeply nested documents and very long values ran off the right edge with no way to reach them.

items.title: Long file names were unreadable in Compare
items.detail: Two files differing only at the end — `orders.a.json` and `orders.b.json` — displayed identically. Names now keep both ends, so the part that tells them apart survives.

items.title: Grid cells could sit on “loading” forever
items.detail: A failed fetch reported nothing and the cells never resolved.

items.title: Error messages say what is actually wrong
items.detail: `parse error: expected value at line 1 column 1` was the same sentence for a stray quote, a bare word and an empty document. You now get “One comma too many”, “The document is cut off”, “A property has no value” — with the offending character marked in a snippet of your own text.

items.title: One-click fixes
items.detail: Where the problem is repairable the message carries a button that applies it and reloads, instead of leaving you to hunt through a long line by hand.

items.title: Opening a YAML, XML, CSV or cURL file offers to convert it
items.detail: Pandia has always done this for pasted text; as a file it used to report a stray byte somewhere in the middle.

items.title: Every way in explains itself
items.detail: Paste, the file picker, drag-and-drop, recent files and URL fetch. Previously only some of them did.

items.title: JSON wrapped in quotes opens as your data
items.detail: In 1.0.4 a document copied out of code, a shell command or a spreadsheet cell — `'{"orderId":917399}'` — loaded as one long piece of text instead of an object. Single quotes, smart quotes and backticks are all understood, at either end or both.

items.title: A stray quote at one end no longer stops the file opening
items.detail: Which is what a slightly-short selection leaves behind.

items.title: Invisible characters before the first bracket no longer break a paste
items.detail: 1.0.4 handled the byte order mark; zero-width spaces, word joiners, direction marks and nulls now go too — the ones that made a file fail with nothing visibly wrong, where deleting a single character you could not see fixed it.

items.title: A failed paste keeps your text
items.detail: Pasting something Pandia could not read used to empty the box, so you had to go back and copy it again.

items.title: NDJSON files round-trip
items.detail: Saving a `.ndjson` or `.jsonl` file writes one record per line again rather than silently rewriting it as a JSON array, and untouched records are written back byte for byte. Save As picks the format from the extension you choose.

items.title: Numbers keep every digit through all of this
items.detail: 64-bit IDs and snowflakes in an NDJSON or JSON5 file stay exact, and multi-gigabyte NDJSON still opens on the streaming path.

items.title: NDJSON and JSON Lines files open
items.detail: A `.ndjson` or `.jsonl` file loads as an array of its records — one value per line, pretty-printed records, blank lines and CRLF all handled — instead of failing with “trailing characters at line 2”.

items.title: JSONC files open
items.detail: Line and block comments and trailing commas are accepted, so a `tsconfig.jsonc` or any commented config loads straight away.

items.title: JSON5 files open
items.detail: Unquoted keys, single-quoted strings, hex numbers, leading and trailing decimal points, `+1`, `Infinity`, `NaN` and escaped line continuations are all understood.

items.title: Files saved with a UTF-8 byte order mark open
items.detail: These are common on Windows and previously failed on the very first character.

items.title: `.jsonl` and `.ndjson` appear in the Open dialog
items.detail: They were missing, so those files could not even be selected. All six extensions now appear in Open, in the recent-files picker and in Compare.

items.title: Undoing back to the last saved state clears the unsaved marker
Settings opens from its own entry in the menu bar
Graph export is a split button
items.detail: Download in your last-used format with one click, or open the menu to pick another.

items.title: Keyboard shortcuts work on Windows and Linux
items.detail: Save, find, new tab, switching views and the rest now fire reliably even where the native menu accelerators did not.

items.title: Shortcut hints read correctly on every platform
items.detail: ⌘, ⇧, ⌥ and ⏎ now show as Ctrl, Shift, Alt and Enter on Windows and Linux across menus, tooltips, the command palette and inline editors.

items.title: Graph panning and zoom are smooth on Windows
items.detail: Mouse-wheel and precision-touchpad scrolling no longer crawls, lurches or overshoots, and Ctrl with +/− zooms even when a touchpad swallows the pinch gesture.

items.title: The traffic light buttons close the app on macOS
items.detail: Closing the window used to need a force quit.

items.title: Big integers stay exact everywhere
items.detail: Editing, duplicating, copying, pasting or filtering a large number — 64-bit IDs, snowflakes — no longer rounds its last digits, including multi-row copy and extract in the grid.

items.title: Grid copy, extract and filter report their errors
items.detail: They used to fail silently.

items.title: Fixed a memory leak from opening and closing many tabs in one session
First stable release — Pandia is now 1.0
